description: Fuse two or more records of the same entity into a new arbitration record. Without arbitration_model use voting, median and union rules; with an arbiter, conflicts may incur LLM cost. Returns output, conflicts, fusion metadata and a new record ID. The merged result can feed linked databases and overwrite current entity values. Inspect database warnings and the actual fusion method; an arbiter failure can fall back to rules. Use this after separately recovered model runs, not to merge different entities. See enricher://docs/enrichment-and-fusion. With arbitration_model='auto' YOU arbitrate (unless use_platform_models=true): the call returns the job status at its first pending request (answer_llm_request) or at the terminal state. A rule-based merge (no arbitration_model) makes no model call and blocks until done.

arbitration_model.description: LLM arbitration: None = rule-based (no model call), 'auto' = YOUR model (or the platform's pick with use_platform_models=true), a platform key = that model.
arbitration_model.title: Arbitration Model

attachment_ids.description: Attachments passed to the arbitration LLM (ignored for rule-based merges).
attachment_ids.title: Attachment Ids

result_ids.description: UUIDs of the enrichment records to merge (minimum 2).
result_ids.title: Result Ids

use_platform_models.description: false (default): every LLM call of this job runs on YOUR model — the job parks each call as a pending request you answer with answer_llm_request; no credits are consumed. true: the job runs on the platform (billed) and, with the model left on auto, on the organization's best model for the task — its highest blended benchmark score under the organization's quality/speed/cost weights, among the models that satisfy the run (attachments, web search, thinking). Naming a platform model also runs the job there, bypassing that pick: do it only when the user named one. Protocol: enricher://docs/llm-delegation.
use_platform_models.title: Use Platform Models

wait_seconds.description: Delegated merges only: how long to wait for the first pending request or completion before returning.
wait_seconds.title: Wait Seconds
